name: Southern Oregon

climate: Pinot Noir sits in its sweet spot, so the wines can show the style it is known for.

terms: American Viticultural Area. A wine labeled with one must take at least 85% of its grapes from that area.
Oregon is stricter than federal law: a wine named for an AVA needs 95% of its grapes from that AVA, and one named for an AVA wholly in Oregon must use only Oregon grapes.

notes: Oregon Pinot Gris is medium bodied, yellow to copper-pink, with aromas of pear, apple and melon.

blurb.text: An AVA in southwest Oregon that takes in the Rogue Valley and Umpqua Valley AVAs. Growers sought it as a name with more meaning to consumers, setting their wines apart from Willamette Valley wines. Pinot Noir is the most planted grape, followed by Pinot Gris, Syrah and Chardonnay.
